heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF PESISIR BARAT REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Central Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds governmental power of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia assisted by the Vice President and ministers as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is West Pesisir Regency.
3. Regional Government is the administration of Governmental Affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
4. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
5. Regent is the Regent of West Pesisir.
6. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a people's representative institution positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
7. Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning hereinafter abbreviated as Dinas PPPAKB is a Regional Apparatus Organization that implements and handles affairs of Protection of Women and Children.
8. Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as PPA is a handling effort to protect and fulfill the rights of women and children from all forms of violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
9. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion either directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
10. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, social, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
13. Violence against women and children in the household is any act against a woman and child that results in suffering or distress physically, sexually, psychologically, economically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household sphere.
14. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
15. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
16. Child marriage is a marriage conducted through civil, religious or customary law with or without registration or official consent where one or both partners are children under the age of 18 years.
17. Woman is a person (human) who has genital organs, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
18. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering either physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or Regional Government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
19. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
20. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 21. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
22. Regional Long-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJPD is a regional development planning document for a period of 20 (twenty) years.
23. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan hereinafter referred to as RPJMD is a regional planning document for a period of 5 (five) years. 24. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Criminal Acts of Trafficking in Persons hereinafter referred to as Task Force is a coordinative institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of criminal acts of trafficking in persons in West Pesisir Regency.
25. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
26. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
28. Child-Friendly Regency is a regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community, business world and media that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights and special protection of children.
29. Private Sector is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media.

Article 5
heading_path: FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 5

Physical violence as referred to in Article 4 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death of women and/or children.

heading: Article 6
heading_path: FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 6

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 4 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.

heading: Article 7
heading_path: FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: Article 8
heading_path: FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 8

Neglect as referred to in Article 4 letter d includes:
a. acts of deliberately neglecting women within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood and care to such women.
b. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care;
c. acts of deliberately neglecting to care for or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care.

heading: Article 9
heading_path: FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: Article 10
heading_path: FORMS OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 10

1. Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and community as referred to in Article 14 letter b and letter c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and community.
2. The form of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in handling victims of violence. (3) The form of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 25

1. The Regional Government shall establish partnerships with the business world in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted through:
a. notification of information on employment opportunities for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.
c. Development of facilities and infrastructure related to the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST PESISIR REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST PESISIR REGENCY

NUMBER 6 YEAR 2022 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST PESISIR REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasing trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are increasingly complex along with the influence of technological developments. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as a protector for its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One effort to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from the potential of acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector holistically and inseparably from one another. Community services are the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. These efforts are carried out with the aim of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 7
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF WEST PESISIR REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 7

a. Non-physical sexual harassment is an act directed at the body, sexual desire, and/or reproductive organs with the intention of degrading the dignity and honor of a person based on their sexuality and/or decency.

The types of non-physical violent behavior include dominant behavior from one party that is controlling, demeaning, intimidating, insulting and harassing both verbally such as speech and non-verbally such as attitude.

b. Physical sexual harassment is any person who commits a sexual act physically directed at the body, sexual desire, and/or reproductive organs with the intention of degrading the dignity and honor of a person based on their sexuality and/or decency. Physical sexual harassment includes unwanted touching, leading to sexual acts such as kissing, patting, pinching, glancing or staring lustfully.

c. Sufficiently clear.

d. Sufficiently Clear.

e. What is meant by forced marriage is child marriage, forced marriage in the name of cultural practices or forced marriage of the Victim to the perpetrator of rape.

f. Sufficiently Clear.

g. Sexual exploitation is an act by violence or threat of violence or by abusing position, authority, trust, acts arising from fraud or relationship of circumstances, vulnerability, inequality, powerlessness, dependence of a person, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits with the intention of obtaining profit, or exploiting the sexual organs or other body organs of that person directed at sexual desire with them or with another person.

h. Sexual slavery is any person who unlawfully places a person under their power or another person's and renders them powerless with the intention of sexually exploiting them.

i. Electronic-based sexual violence is an act that without right conducts recording and/or taking pictures or screenshots containing sexual content outside the will or without the consent of the person who is the object of the recording or picture or screenshot, transmitting electronic information and/or electronic documents containing sexual content outside the will of the recipient directed at sexual desire and/or conducting stalking and/or tracking using electronic systems against the person who is the object in the electronic information/document for sexual purposes is criminalized for committing violence.
